guide.title: Copper hammers: when to use one, and how to choose
guide.lead: A copper hammer is a soft face hammer: it strikes firmly but gives way before the part does. Here is when to reach for one, how copper compares with brass, nylon and dead-blow hammers, and what to look for when you buy.

s1.title: What a copper hammer is for
s1.p1: A copper hammer — sometimes called a copper mallet — is built for soft-face striking. The copper face is softer than hardened steel, so when it meets a bearing race, a shaft end or a machined surface, the copper deforms first and the part keeps its shape.
s1.p2: That makes it the hammer for assembly and alignment: seating bearings and bushings, tapping workpieces into a vice, driving dowel pins, nudging a housing into line or freeing a seized part without leaving a mark. It is also why copper is often called a bearing hammer in maintenance workshops.

s2.title: Copper vs brass vs nylon vs dead-blow
s2.p1: Soft face hammers trade hardness for protection. The softer the face, the less it marks — and the less force it transmits.
s2.caption: Soft face hammer types compared

copper.use: Bearings, shafts, pins, assembly and alignment

brass.use: Drifts and punches on softer steels, general maintenance

nylon.use: Sheet metal, finished and painted surfaces, light assembly

deadblow.use: Seating parts where bounce-back must be avoided

s2.p2: Copper sits in the middle: it transmits more of the blow than nylon or rubber, marks far less than steel or brass and has little rebound.

s3.title: Does copper spark?
s3.p1: Copper does not produce the hot sparks steel does when struck, which is why copper tools are used near flammables. People often search for a "non-sparking hammer" for exactly this reason.
s3.p2: But certified tools for explosive atmospheres are tested and approved separately; a copper hammer is not automatically approved for Ex-zones. Check your site's explosion-protection document before you use any hammer in a hazardous area.

s4.title: Choosing a weight
items: 300–500 g for fine assembly: small pins, instrument housings, light alignment.
500–800 g for general workshop use: bearings, bushings, vices and fixtures.
1 kg and more for heavy seating: large bearings, couplings and big housings.
s4.p1: At 620 g, Premium Hammer sits in the general-workshop range.

s5.title: Handle materials
items: Wood (ash, hickory): light and warm in the hand, but varnished wood slips in oil and can loosen as it dries out.
Fibreglass: durable and damping; usually covered in a rubber or plastic sleeve that can go slippery in oil.
Composite: glass- or carbon-reinforced polymer, often with an elastomer grip; behaviour in oil varies with the grip.
Aluminium carbon: a stiff, light shaft that keeps the weight in the head; with a knurled metal grip it holds in oil, emulsion and water.

s6.title: Caring for a copper hammer
s6.p1: Copper is meant to give, so the face will mushroom with use. Keep the head clean and dry. Dress light burrs and mushrooming with a file to restore a flat face.
s6.p2: Replace the hammer — or the head, where the design allows — when the face is badly deformed, cracked, or the head loosens on the handle.

who.title: Who we are
who.body: Tomstroj d.o.o. — in full, an engineering, machine-building and trading company — designs and builds machines and mechanical systems from its base in Notranje Gorice, with a second workshop in Vrhnika. The work runs from engineering and design to fabrication, hydraulics, electrics and assembly.

building.title: What we're building
building.body: Alongside contract engineering, Tomstroj develops its own products. The first is TIFCO, a mobile waste compactor for hotels and commercial kitchens: it runs on a standard single-phase socket, compacts a full bag in about 30 seconds and drops the compacted waste straight into the bin. TIFCO is in final testing.

why.title: Why a hammer
why.body: Assembly work needs a hammer that strikes firmly without marking bearings, shafts or finished parts. The copper hammers we could buy had heavy wooden handles that slipped in oil. So we made our own: a copper head, an aluminium carbon shaft and a machined grip. Other workshops asked for one. Premium Hammer is the result — one product, made properly.

imprint.disputesBody: We sell to businesses only. We are neither obliged nor willing to take part in consumer dispute resolution proceedings.

sections.p: TOMSTROJ, podjetje za inženiring, strojegradnjo in trgovino d.o.o., Podovnice 1, 1357 Notranje Gorice, Slovenia. Email: tomstroj@siol.net, phone: +386 41 588 114.

When you use the order, dealer or contact form we process the data you enter: company name, VAT ID, contact name, email address, phone number, delivery country and address, engraving text and your message. For spam protection and rate limiting we briefly process your IP address.

We use form data to process orders and enquiries: to prepare an order confirmation and invoice, to arrange delivery and to answer your questions. The legal basis is the performance of a contract or steps prior to a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and our legitimate interest in answering business enquiries and protecting the site from abuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). We check VAT IDs against the EU VIES service to apply the correct VAT treatment (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR).

Order data and invoices are kept for as long as Slovenian tax and accounting law requires (generally 10 years after the end of the year the invoice was issued). Enquiries that do not lead to an order are deleted within 24 months. Rate-limit data is held in memory for at most one hour.

Resend (email delivery), Vercel (hosting and cookieless, aggregated analytics) and Cloudflare Turnstile (spam protection). Each acts on our behalf under a data processing agreement. Some processors may process data outside the EU under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or the EU–US Data Privacy Framework.

We use Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights, which are cookieless and do not track you across sites. We do not use tracking cookies, so no cookie banner is needed. Cloudflare Turnstile may set a strictly necessary cookie when you submit a form.

You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and objection, and the right to withdraw consent. You can lodge a complaint with the Slovenian Information Commissioner (Informacijski pooblaščenec, www.ip-rs.si).
For any privacy question, email tomstroj@siol.net.
